idiom_name: as_/to_/into_ conversions, bare getter names, #[must_use] queries
implementation_notes: The Rust API Guidelines make the method name state cost and ownership, which is exactly what a caller needs: `as_` is a free borrowed view (`str::as_bytes`), `to_` allocates or computes (`Path::to_str`, `str::to_lowercase`), `into_` consumes the receiver (`String::into_bytes`), getters use the bare field name (`slice::first`, `first_mut`) with `get` reserved for a single obvious value (`Cell::get`), and the `TempDir::path` versus `into_path` pair shows the difference between borrowing a property and taking responsibility for cleanup. Types carry the rest: `#[must_use]` marks a query whose result cannot be ignored, newtypes (`struct UserId(u64)`) stop two identically typed values from being swapped, and `Result`-returning constructors state that failure is possible. Keep a `get_`-prefixed name only for the genuine single-obvious-value case or to mirror an FFI/collection API (`HashMap::get`).
pitfalls: A `to_` that is actually free or an `as_` that allocates makes the name lie about cost, and callers will chain it in a hot loop; keep the prefixes literal and add `_unchecked` variants instead of hiding validation inside `get`.
A public field freezes the representation into the API forever: use private fields plus `fn lines(&self) -> &[OrderLine]`, and expose mutation only through named operations (`&mut self`).

`#[must_use]` on the type is easy to forget when a query returns a wrapper, so an ignored `Money` or `Result` compiles silently; enable `clippy::let_underscore_must_use` and return types, not primitives.
